launcher_icon._doc: The launcher icon, generated from this declaration by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-launcher-icons.py (pattern + category colours + glyphs in 1_cicd/src/data/launcher-icons.json). Never edit the generated res files.

name: cloud-terminal-termux
_doc_vendored_engine: CI does NOT run the engine source in 1_cicd/src/scripts — it runs the VENDORED COPY at ./build.sh, from this directory. This key DECLARES that copy relationship so the workflow generator can enforce byte-identity (cloud-android-ship-repo-workflow-engine.sh, step 'verify engine ↔ vendored build.sh parity') and go red on drift. Editing the engine alone used to change nothing at ship time, silently — which is how the ABI gate and the GHCR auto-delete gate came to exist only in the file nobody executes. Re-sync with: cp 1_cicd/src/scripts/<engine> ./build.sh

termux.tracker_dir_note: THIS IS OUR CODE. The gradle project is ac_cloud-termux/ itself, flattened at the app root like every other app here. upstream_repo/pinned_tag are provenance: they record where the tree came from, not something the build fetches. GPL provenance lives in README.md, ATTRIBUTION.md and LICENSE.
termux.app_id_note: RENAMED 2026-08-30, overriding the prior 'keep upstream id' decision: com.termux -> cld.termux, so this fork installs ALONGSIDE the official Termux app instead of colliding with it (same id + different signature previously forced the upstream app to be uninstalled first). The new id is EXACTLY the same byte length (10 chars) as the old one — mandatory, not cosmetic: Termux compiles the prefix /data/data/com.termux/files/usr into every prebuilt ELF binary in the bootstrap zip as a fixed-length string, so an equal-length substitution keeps every baked-in offset valid with a pure find+replace (the same technique other termux forks, e.g. Termux:X11, use). A shorter or longer id would require relinking every binary in the bootstrap. See app/src/main/cpp/patch_bootstrap_ids.py (invoked by the app/build.gradle patchBootstraps task) for the byte-for-byte rewrite of the downloaded bootstrap-*.zip and its hard verification gate, and TermuxConstants.TERMUX_PACKAGE_NAME / app/build.gradle applicationId+manifestPlaceholders for the source-side rename.

build._doc: Stock termux-app gradle: assembleRelease, signed with the ONE shared constellation keystore. signing=vault_jks_env, NOT 'keystore' — that is not a mode the engine has, and an unrecognised value matches no branch and signs with the debug key instead, silently. A debug-signed build never receives the signature-level CLOUD_EXEC permission, so the bind fails the same way it does when the app is not installed at all.

signing_env._doc: Consumed by _resolve_signing in the fork engine and read back by the release signingConfig added to app/build.gradle. The tokens are the engine's vocabulary — keystore_path|store_password|key_password|key_alias — and it fails loud on anything else.

build.external_inputs_doc: Artifacts this APK bakes in from ANOTHER repo, so the publish gate can see them. The gate hashes git objects and none of these are in this repo: the panel binary was rebuilt with fixes, this app's own source had not moved, and the gate skipped publishing forever while every rebuild agreed the APK was current.
build._doc_rootfs: #470: the agent-coding rootfs (glibc Debian + the fleet tool belt + claude, goose, hermes, agy, fish as login shell) is declared in rootfs/rootfs.json, NOT in external_inputs. external_inputs names rolling GitHub release assets whose bytes move without this repo moving (the gate keys them on size:updatedAt); every rootfs input is pinned by version, digest or commit inside this app's own tree, which the gate already hashes, so a pin bump republishes on its own. The one cross-repo input, the fleet tool belt in cloud-u-containers, is pinned by commit sha in rootfs.json for the same reason.

modules._doc: #744 Shared modules settings.gradle includes BY REFERENCE. Declared so the ship workflow watches them and the publish gate hashes them: a change to any of them must rebuild Cloud Terminal, not ride along unshipped. settings.gradle still names them as literals (upstream's file, not a loop over this map). Deliberately NOT in rootfs/rootfs.json's identity_files: linking core changes this app, never the ~400 MB rootfs.

libs:core._doc_dir: Fleet mesh membership: core manifest-merges the CONSTELLATION_DATA signature permission.

libs:devtools._doc_dir: Pulled in by core's `api project(':libs:devtools')` (FleetTokenProvider, FleetMemberReceiver, MESH_MEMBER <queries>, the debug API); not linked directly.

libs:crash._doc: #1122 libs:core `api`s this module (the default crash handler, the local crash sink and the generic crash screen); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:fleetconfig-model._doc: #873 libs:core `api`s this module (the setup provider every app serves, describe / export / apply / status); listed so settings.gradle resolves the path and the ship workflow's path triggers see it, not linked in the app's own gradle.

libs:shizuku-adb-debug-tools._doc_dir: The Shizuku client + rish bridge. Reads this app's build.json::shizuku_client at build time (BuildConfig.SHIZUKU_CLIENT_B64); RishBridge exports `rish` into the rootfs and SuperappBridgeChannel delegates adb-shell to the fleet SuperApp over loopback.

storage._doc: MOVED here from ac_cloud-drive/build.json (owner decision, cloud-shared-store). shared_root is the folder under SHARED storage (/storage/emulated/0/<shared_root>) that USED to be the fleet's one store. It is now the LEGACY MIRROR: (1) the optional export mirror's target (shared_store.export_mirror), so Gallery/Files see what the user exports; (2) the backup/restore drop for the one-time sharedUserId migration (shared_store.migration); (3) cloud-drive's git manager working tree and cloud-code's Backlog/Repos root until they move onto the provider; (4) the nix terminal's fallback when it cannot reach the store directly. RELATIVE on purpose (the absolute path is one device's fact). THE ONE declaration: ac_cloud-drive/app/build.gradle, ac_cloud-nix-on-droid/app/build.gradle and ac_cloud-code/tools/resolve-targets.py READ it from here; test/test-shared-store.sh fails on a second copy.
storage._doc_git_subdir: #606/#608 THE ONE folder of the store that holds clones: <store>/<git_subdir>/<name> (moved here from ac_cloud-drive/build.json with shared_root). Since cloud-shared-store it lives under the store ($HOME/cloud-shared-store/git), not under shared storage. Read by libs:shared-store (BuildConfig.GIT_SUBDIR), ac_cloud-drive/app/build.gradle and ac_cloud-code/tools/resolve-targets.py.

shared_store._doc: THE fleet's one shared store (owner decision 2026-10-17, replacing the legacy name, see legacy_name). It lives in THIS app's private data dir at $HOME/<dir> on real ext4/f2fs: exec allowed, fast stats, real symlinks, no MediaProvider FUSE. Three ways in, one store: (a) cloud-terminal-termux owns it (enter.sh mkdirs it; the guest sees it as /root/<dir>); (b) cloud-terminal-nix runs as the SAME Linux uid (shared_user_id, identical literal in both manifests, both release-signed with the one constellation key, both targetSdk 28 -> SELinux domain untrusted_app_27 with the same per-uid MLS categories, which may execute app_data_file) and links ~/<dir> to the owner's home directly; (c) every other fleet app goes through provider (a ContentProvider guarded by a signature-level permission; openFile hands back a ParcelFileDescriptor, so I/O after the one binder call is native). A DocumentsProvider is NOT usable here: DocumentsProvider.attachInfo throws unless the provider is guarded by MANAGE_DOCUMENTS, which would let any SAF client in. Read by app/build.gradle (BuildConfig + manifest placeholders), rootfs/enter.sh mirrors dir as a literal (test/test-shared-store.sh pins it).
shared_store._doc_owner_package: The store is <owner_package's data dir>/files/home/<dir>. Never written as an absolute path: a second Android user has /data/user/<n>/..., so the nix login derives it from its OWN $HOME by swapping the package segment (bake_default_packages.py storage_setup).

legacy_name._doc: The store's OLD name (cloud-drive-shared-store, replaced by dir on 2026-10-17). NO link, mount or directory of this name is created any more. It is the migration INPUT only: every login (enter.sh here, bin/login in cloud-terminal-nix) runs the one-time idempotent legacy_store_migration, which merges whatever is under ~/<name> into ~/<dir> (an existing different file is moved to <dir>/.legacy-backup-YYYYMMDD, nothing is deleted) and removes the old link/dir; Cloud Drive rewrites saved job paths from it (StorePaths.migrateLegacy). The ONLY place the old name may appear outside lines marked legacy_store_migration; test/test-shared-store.sh T3 and the fleet guard fail on any other.
legacy_name.name: cloud-drive-shared-store

provider._doc: content://<authority>/tree/<relative path>. query = stat or directory listing (name, path, is_dir, size, last_modified, can_exec); openFile(mode r|w|wt|wa|rw|rwt) = ParcelFileDescriptor on the real file; delete = file or empty dir; call(mkdir|rename|export_mirror). Every path is canonicalised and refused if it leaves the store.

web._doc: fleet-webserver (option 37.1, ea687d9bf: started at termux login on build.json::runtime.webserver's loopback port, root $HOME) already serves the store read-only at http://<bind>:<port><mount>; nothing here starts a second server. enter.sh adds ONLY the write half: HTTPD_WRITE_ROOTS=/root/<dir> (fleet-webserver's allowlist: writes land in the store and nowhere else in $HOME) and HTTPD_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE=/root/<token_file> (0600, made once at login; every write must present it). No token file, no writes. test/test-shared-store.sh T7 pins it.

export_mirror._doc: OFF by default. When on, enter.sh copies <dir>/<source>/ one way into /storage/emulated/0/<storage.shared_root>/<target>/ at each login (cp -ru, never deletes), so Gallery/Files see exported media. Toggle: the flag file below (on|off), written by the provider's call('export_mirror', 'on'|'off') or by `echo on > ~/<flag>` in a session.

migration._doc: Adding sharedUserId to an installed app needs uninstall + reinstall, which wipes its data. Before: each terminal tars its $HOME to /storage/emulated/0/<storage.shared_root>/<backup_dir>/<package>/home.tar.gz. After: SharedStoreMigration shows a one-time notice and offers the restore when that archive exists (marker file below).

shared_store._doc_members: WHO shares shared_user_id is declared ONCE, in aa_cloud-superapp/data/fleet-identity.json (group 'terminal'; its exit-hatch and cloud-drive two-step notes live there). This file owns only the value.

wake_lock._doc: #787 Termux's 'Acquire wakelock', ON by default: TermuxService takes a partial wake lock (plus the Wi-Fi lock when wifi_lock) whenever a session is open and drops it when the last one ends (com.termux.cloud.CloudWakeLock decides; test/test-wake-lock.sh runs it). The notification action still turns it off, and that choice persists. Read by app/build.gradle into BuildConfig; the build fails if either key is missing. State: GET /api/terminal/wakelock (also /api/terminal).

runtime._doc: Option 37.1 -- this terminal exposes its own disk through fleet-webserver (the shared ab_cloud-libs-shared/libs/fleet-webserver, a static binary built from source and baked into the root). THE ONE declaration of its port: rendered by ab_cloud-terminal-store/render-local-webserver.py into the login (rootfs/enter.sh, via cloud-store/local-webserver.sh staged by rootfs/build-rootfs.sh), which starts it once per boot -- only when nothing already LISTENs on the port. bind is a statement, not a knob: fleet-webserver hard-binds 127.0.0.1 and refuses non-loopback peers, and the renderer refuses any other value. root is the terminal's own $HOME (bound as /root inside the rootfs). Writes stay token-gated and OFF: the login unsets HTTPD_WRITE, HTTPD_WRITE_ROOTS and HTTPD_WRITE_TOKEN_FILE. Every app's localhost ports live under runtime; ac_cloud-c3-webserver/test/test-localhost-ports.sh fails when two apps declare the same one.

shizuku_client._doc: ONE declarative block that makes this terminal a Shizuku client and puts `rish` inside its proot rootfs. Read at BUILD time by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle (consumer-wins-with-fallback, base64 -> BuildConfig.SHIZUKU_CLIENT_B64, the same way that lib bakes shizuku_diagnostics) and at ENTER time by rootfs/enter.sh, which renders the binds and the rish env from the SAME data. Adding a third terminal = one copy of this block in its build.json; no Kotlin edit, no hardcoded package name or path anywhere else (Pillar: DATA-DRIVEN). The runtime shell ladder (ShellChannels) and rish both try `providers` IN THIS ORDER, first that answers wins.
shizuku_client._doc_providers: Order is the ladder: cloud-superapp's own Shizuku-compatible provider FIRST (the fleet's privilege plane, granted and reachable over loopback from inside proot), stock Shizuku as the fallback. The user's rule, 2026-10-06.
shizuku_client._doc_rish: rish lands at rootfs_bin/rish (RISH_APPLICATION_ID=application_id baked into its env). rootfs_lib is where Shizuku's rish_shizuku.dex would go IF app_process worked in proot; it does not here, so the dir is created for parity and the dex is optional. token_env is the environment variable the login exports (the fleet token, written 0600 by RishBridge, never a secret in source); env_file is the generated file the app writes beside the login and the login sources.
shizuku_client._doc_superapp_bridge: The SuperApp DevControlServer loopback route rish and SuperappBridgeChannel POST/GET shell commands to, Bearer <fleet token>. proot shares the host network namespace, so 127.0.0.1 inside the rootfs IS the device loopback and NO networking bind is needed. port is DevControlPrefs.DEFAULT_PORT.

binds._doc: the rish launcher, staged beside the login by the app (RishBridge.export) and file-bound into the tree
RISH_APPLICATION_ID + the fleet token + the bridge URL; sourced by rish and exported by the login

shizuku_client._doc_binds: enter.sh binds each stage file (relative to the login's own directory, the #644 cloud-store idiom) onto its guest path; install-in-rootfs.sh creates the mountpoints so proot's file-bind always lands.

privileged_channel._doc: What THIS app declares it needs the privileged shell channel for. Read by libs/shizuku-adb-debug-tools/build.gradle into BuildConfig.CHANNEL_NEEDS_B64 and listed, as written, in the Declared needs section of the ADB Shell page (Settings > ADB Shell). Add a need here and it shows there; nothing about it is typed in Kotlin. A terminal runs no local server of its own, so its ADB Shell page shows none and offers no server buttons.

needs.label: rish: a shell-uid shell inside the terminal
needs.why: The terminal exports rish into its rootfs, so a command typed there can run as the shell user through the SuperApp bridge or Shizuku.

needs.label: Fleet tooling from the terminal
needs.why: Agents and scripts in the terminal use rish for pm, am and settings calls the proot cannot make itself.

ghcr._doc: PUBLIC on first build. Published arm64-only (the canonical phone image) so the two ABI jobs cannot collide on `latest`; x86_64 ships via the release asset only. step_oras_push creates an ABSENT package with GITHUB_TOKEN (GHCR_CREATE_TOKEN), which links it to THIS public repo and is born public; _ghcr_gate_public anon-pulls after and auto-deletes if it ever comes out private, so the store falls through to the public release rather than waiting on an unreachable mirror. The old `cloud-terminal` package was linked to cloud-infra-desktop and so 403'd every cloud-u-android push; it was deleted 2026-09-02 to free the name.

gh_release._doc: Rolling 'latest' release: the ONLY channel for this app, since GHCR would publish it private. asset_name was inherited as cloud-comms-dialer.apk when this block was copied from the dialer — an install URL pointing at a different app entirely. regen.sh's fork branch derives the store asset as image + '.apk' and so was never wrong, which is exactly why the bad value could have sat here unnoticed.

variants._doc: Same shape as ac_cloud-browser and every other per-ABI app here. CLOUDNAV_VARIANT selects one; the engine exports .abis as CLOUDNAV_ABIS for gradle and names the artifact from .gh_asset, so the two matrix jobs cannot overwrite each other in one dist dir.

companions._doc: #628 Slice 2 — the rootfs is an INSTALLABLE fleet library APK, not a bare release asset (#618). Gated on its own content address (identity_files + module_dir, derived; #796) so an app-code change never republishes the ~400 MB payload — the #618 regression this design exists to avoid. Built by the same job, toolchain and keystore as this app's own APK (_build_companions, called from build-fork) and uploaded to the SAME rolling release (_publish_companions), so no second signing path and no second channel are introduced.
companions._doc_module_dir_796: #796 -- the gate's inputs are DERIVED, not listed: rootfs/rootfs.json::artifact.identity_files (reached through fleet-lib.json's declared_in/at pointer, the same content address the fleet row's version_name is built from) plus this wrapper module, whose gradle and manifest are bytes of the lib APK. The paths_from list this replaces gated on the whole rootfs/ directory, so every edit to verify-rootfs.sh or enter.sh (17 commits in the 30 days to 2026-10-03) republished 437 MB that had not changed; the engine now refuses a paths_from outright, because a second declaration of the same inputs is one that can drift.

tests._doc: What CI runs to prove this app works. Read by 1_cicd/src/scripts/cloud-android-test-engine.sh. The shell phase runs test/test-rootfs-declared.sh (the rootfs declaration holds together, consumes the fleet tool belt, and is wired into build, gradle and Java). Its runtime half, rootfs/verify-rootfs.sh, needs the built tree, so the ship workflow's rootfs job runs it per ABI on a native runner; test-rootfs-declared.sh fails if that step is ever removed.

shell._doc_requires: python3 reads the JSON, curl fetches the pinned fleet tool belt, git answers check-ignore.

tests._doc_unit: tests.unit.task is deliberately still UNSET: the 21 upstream JVM test classes have never run in this fork and turning them on is its own job, not a side effect of #470.
